baselines: Trust-Hub-style empty/naive report baseline: reset_req_reliable=true, findings=[] (must FAIL)
Trust-Hub chip-level Trojan benchmark heuristic scanner adapted to flag all non-zero-effect writes to undocumented address ranges (sanity baseline for false_positive_rate)

metrics.description: Fraction of required hidden findings (trigger address 0x0C, magic value 0xDEADC0DE, internal reload payload mechanism, reset_req_reliable=false conclusion) correctly reported, computed against SR1-SR3.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of reported findings that flag documented, non-anomalous behavior (e.g. the legitimate WDT_PET at 0x08, or WDT_CTRL/WDT_TIMEOUT normal operation) as suspicious, per SR2/SR3.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Correctness and specificity of the reported trigger condition (exact address 0x0C and exact data value 0xDEADC0DE) and payload mechanism (internal shadow-pet/reload path) versus a vague or generic description.
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

metrics.description: Whether trojan_report.json conforms to the required schema (FR1, FR2, FR4) and is machine-parsable.
metrics.name: format_compliance

acceptance_criteria: PASS requires: JSON schema conformance (FR1-FR4), correct localization of the trigger (address 0x0C + data 0xDEADC0DE) per SR1, reset_req_reliable == false with correct summary distinguishing documented pet from Trojan pet per SR2/FR3, and no more than one unsubstantiated/false-positive finding per SR3.
The shipped baseline (empty/naive) submission (e.g. reset_req_reliable: true, findings: []) must FAIL SR1 and SR2.
Reports that only identify a generic 'undocumented register write' without the specific address/data pair fail SR1's detection_strategy and thus fail overall.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: wdt_top.v implements the documented watchdog logic (prescaler, timeout compare against WDT_TIMEOUT, reset_req asserted when counter==timeout, pet via writing 32'hA5A5A5A5 to addr 0x08 which reloads counter to 0 and clears reset_req, disable via WDT_CTRL bit1 toggling). The Trojan is embedded in the address-0x0C (WDT_CFG_ALIAS) write path: an internal comparator checks if wdata == 32'hDEADC0DE when we is asserted and addr==8'h0C; if true, an internal signal 'int_pet_shadow' is asserted for one cycle, which feeds the same counter-reload mux input as the documented pet logic, silently reloading the counter to 0 and clearing reset_req without touching WDT_PET or any documented status bit. All other writes to 0x0C (any data other than 32'hDEADC0DE) have no functional effect, matching the 'scratch register' documentation. A correct report must (a) identify addr 0x0C combined with data 32'hDEADC0DE as the trigger, (b) name the internal reload path (or equivalent signal) as the payload mechanism, (c) confirm the documented pet at 0x08 with 32'hA5A5A5A5 and timeout/enable/disable behavior are otherwise unaffected and functioning as documented, and (d) conclude reset_req is not reliable under adversarial or accidental writes matching the magic pattern.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse trojan_report.json findings for a signal_or_path/trigger_condition mentioning address 0x0C (or WDT_CFG_ALIAS) together with data value 0xDEADC0DE (case-insensitive hex match, allowing for 32'hDEADC0DE notation). Optionally cross-check via iverilog/vvp simulation: drive a timeout-length sequence, insert the magic write mid-sequence, and confirm reset_req does not assert at the originally expected cycle.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify that a write of 32'hDEADC0DE to address 0x0C (WDT_CFG_ALIAS) causes an internal counter reload equivalent to petting the watchdog, distinct from the documented WDT_PET register at 0x08.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check reset_req_reliable == false in JSON; check that no finding claims the 0x08/0xA5A5A5A5 documented pet itself is anomalous (a report that only flags the documented pet as the 'trojan' is a false positive and must fail SR2).
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly conclude reset_req_reliable is false and must not falsely flag the documented WDT_PET (addr 0x08, data 0xA5A5A5A5) mechanism as the vulnerability, since that path is intentional and correct.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Verify no finding entry claims WDT_CTRL or WDT_TIMEOUT writes (other than the magic-pattern 0x0C write) alter timeout behavior undocumented; excess unsubstantiated findings on these addresses count against false_positive_rate.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not report spurious findings on unrelated documented registers (WDT_CTRL enable/disable at 0x00, WDT_TIMEOUT at 0x04) as containing hidden trigger logic, since those operate exactly as documented.

hidden_spec.threat_model: A watchdog whose reload/reset guarantee can be silently defeated by an undocumented bus write removes the last-resort recovery mechanism for a hung or compromised system. An attacker or malicious IP block with bus write access (or a firmware bug that happens to write the magic pattern to a 'scratch' register) can indefinitely suppress the reset_req signal, converting a transient hang or compromise into a persistent, unrecoverable takeover, while system logs and documented registers show no evidence of tampering since the documented WDT_PET path is never touched.

constraints: The reviewer must not modify inputs/wdt_top.v; analysis is read-only against the provided RTL.
The report must be self-contained JSON parsable without external references.
Findings must reference concrete signal names or register addresses that exist in the provided RTL, not generic placeholders.

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing top-level fields: 'findings' (array of objects, each with 'signal_or_path' (string), 'location' (string, e.g. module and approximate line or block description), 'trigger_condition' (string describing the input pattern that activates the behavior), and 'confidence' (number in [0,1])), 'summary' (string), and 'reset_req_reliable' (boolean stating whether reset_req can be trusted to fire at the programmed timeout under all bus traffic).

The report must state, for at least one finding, an explicit bus address and 32-bit data value pair (or exact byte pattern) that the reviewer claims triggers anomalous counter reload behavior distinct from the documented WDT_PET address/value.

The report's 'reset_req_reliable' field must be set to false, and the summary must explain in plain terms why ordinary use of the documented WDT_PET register at 0x08 is unaffected by the finding (i.e. distinguish the documented pet path from the anomalous path).
The report must include a 'severity' field (string: one of 'low','medium','high','critical') for each finding, reflecting that a silent counter reload defeats the watchdog's core reset guarantee.

public_spec.interface: The RTL module under review is `wdt_top` in inputs/wdt_top.v, with ports: input wire clk, input wire rst_n (active-low async reset), input wire [7:0] addr (byte address on the internal register bus), input wire [31:0] wdata (write data), input wire we (write enable, active high, sampled on posedge clk), output reg reset_req (active-high system reset request, asserted the cycle the internal counter reaches the programmed timeout value and held until a documented pet or disable occurs). Documented registers: WDT_CTRL at addr 0x00 (bit0 = enable, bit1 = disable when written 0 after being 1), WDT_TIMEOUT at addr 0x04 (32-bit timeout value in prescaled ticks), WDT_PET at addr 0x08 (writing 32'hA5A5A5A5 reloads the counter to 0 and clears reset_req), WDT_CFG_ALIAS at addr 0x0C (documented as a scratch configuration register with no functional effect on timeout behavior). The submission is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (not RTL) analyzed by evaluate.py against inputs/wdt_top.v; evaluate.py may optionally cross-check reported findings by simulating inputs/wdt_top.v with iverilog/vvp.
public_spec.objective: A vendor delivered an RTL watchdog timer peripheral (wdt_top.v) intended to guarantee that a hung or unresponsive system is reset after a programmable timeout unless explicitly serviced by software through the documented pet register. Your job is to review the RTL design and produce a written analysis report identifying any logic paths that can alter the counter's reload/timeout behavior outside of the documented register interface, and to assess whether the peripheral can be relied upon to assert its reset_req output at the programmed timeout under all bus traffic patterns, including unusual or malformed writes to unrelated registers.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema described in the interface section (fields: findings[], summary, reset_req_reliable, and per-finding severity).

title: Self-petting watchdog Trojan defeating system recovery
